## The project

<h3>Hackathon Mobilités 2026 -- Spécial Dataviz'</h3>


- Use <a href="https://data.iledefrance-mobilites.fr/explore/?disjunctive.theme&disjunctive.keyword&disjunctive.publisher&disjunctive.modified&disjunctive.features&disjunctive.language&sort=modified">data</a> and data visualisation to explore mobility questions in Île-de-France
- optional data repository (<a href="https://opendata.paris.fr/">open data Paris</a> and <a href="http://wwW.insee.fr">Insee</a>)
- 4 ex questions but you may find another 
- Goal: build visualisations / dashboard that answer a question and could become tools for users or mobility stakeholders


## Challenge #1 -- Mobility and climate adaptation

*Explore the data to understand how heat influences mobility, and give keys to help adapt mobility to climate change.*

<ul>
<li>Did Franciliens stay home more during the heat waves?</li>
<li>Did they use their car more?</li>
<li>Was the transport supply impacted?</li>
</ul>
Use case : 2026 Heatwaves.

## Challenge #2 -- Mobility and employment

*Explore the link between mobility and access to employment, and analyse to what extent transport networks meet the needs.*

<ul>
<li>How do public transport networks make it possible to reach the places where jobs are created and concentrated?</li>
</ul>

## Challenge #3 -- Mobility and impacts on territories

*Use data visualisation to assess the impact of line extensions already completed, and to anticipate or question future transformations of territories.*

<ul>
<li>How do territories change with these new services?</li>
<li>What was the impact on bus trips in these territories?</li>
</ul>

Use case : Line 14.

## Challenge #4 -- Mobility and inequalities

*Make visible, thanks to data, mobility inequalities related to gender, income and place of residence, and imagine representations that inspire more inclusive policies.*

<ul>
<li>Is everyday mobility designed for the diversity of life paths?</li>
<li>How does gender influence travel practices, access to services and facilities, and mobility constraints?</li>
<li>How can we picture more inclusive and more equitable networks?</li>
</ul>

## Assessment

<ul>
<li>1 written exam</li>
<li>1 open project (IDFM hackathon subject)</li>
<li>LLM usage policy for the project</li>
</ul>

## AI tools -- usage policy for the project

<ul>
<li><b>Authorized use</b>: help with code, documentation, ideation -- not for generating final results without human verification</li>
<li><b>Public discussions</b>: share the links to your LLM conversations ; their evaluation is part of the final grade</li>
<li><b>Model</b>: Claude Sonnet as the reference model ; Gemini or GPT accepted in their free version</li>
</ul>


## AI tools -- usage policy for the project

<ul>
<li><b>Responsibility</b>: the student remains the author of the final deliverable</li>
<li><b>Result validation</b>: any result obtained with the help of an LLM must be tested before being kept</li>
<li><b>No AI</b>: choosing not to use AI is perfectly fine ; in case of doubt about the deliverable, oral defense via Zoom</li>
</ul>


## Evaluating the chats -- possible grid (1/2)

<ul>
<li><b>Prompting quality</b>: clear questions, context given (data, goal, constraints), logical iterations rather than scattered attempts</li>
<li><b>Critical thinking</b>: challenges the answers, spots errors and approximations, reformulates instead of copy-pasting</li>
<li><b>Relevance of use</b>: the LLM is used where it adds value (unblocking, exploring ideas), not to avoid thinking ; the student's own contribution is visible</li>
</ul>

## Evaluating the chats -- possible grid (2/2)

<ul>
<li><b>Validation</b>: code is run, numbers and charts are checked against the data</li>
<li><b>Transparency and consistency</b>: complete conversations (no truncated or selective links), consistent with the final deliverable</li>
</ul>

## Deliverable 
Groups of 4 students :

<ul>
<li> (shiny) dashboard </li>
<li> R code (github repos)
<li> report</li>
<li> +LLM discussions links</li>
</ul>
